summary: POC scoping call to decide Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private for Orion Insights' ingestion + customer support LLM features. Discussed workload sizing (RPS, token lengths), success criteria (latency p95 <= 800ms, throughput, quality/regression thresholds), benchmark plan, security/compliance constraints (SOC2, VPC, KMS), and timeline for a 4-6 week pilot. Action items: send pricing, benchmark harness, provide traffic traces, schedule follow-up demo for Dedicated.
topics: Deployment mode decision criteria: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private
transcript:
[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Jordan from Redwood, and with me is Priya our SE and Liam from solutions. Uh quick roll call?
[00:12] Maya: Hi this is Maya, Head of ML at Orion.
[00:15] Ethan: Ethan here, CTO.
[00:17] Priya K: Priya Kapoor, security.
[00:20] Samir: Samir Patel, platform engineer.
[00:25] Jordan: Great. The goal for today is to scope a POC so you can evaluate hosted vs dedicated vs private, figure out success criteria, and then agree timelines. Priya, do you want to give a quick context on the product you plan to build?
[00:35] Maya: Sure, so we're building an LLM-powered customer support assistant that ingests conversation context and product docs. Latency is important because agents are using it in live workflows, we target under like, um, 1 second p50 and p95 under 800 to 1,200ms maybe, but we'll see. Also we need accuracy for retrieval augmented responses, and we want tight cost control - we process roughly 80 million tokens a month today in the prototype.
[01:05] Ethan: From infra side, we want to know what'd be the unit economics of Hosted vs Dedicated, and whether we need full Private (VPC) given that some tickets contain PII and some healthcare-adjacent info.
[01:20] Priya Malhotra (SE): Okay thanks. A few clarifying Qs on workload: what's the concurrent QPS during peak, and average token lengths per request?
[01:30] Maya: Peak is around 120 QPS, average request is about 120 tokens out + 40 tokens in, some prompts go to 700 tokens for long context. We also have spikes — during incidents it can double for short periods.
[01:45] Samir: The traffic is regional, mostly NA and EU, and data residency matters for EU customers. We'll need SSO and audit logs.
[01:55] Priya K (Security): On compliance, SOC2 is table stakes, we also have contracts that reference KMS control for encryption in flight and at rest and key rotation. Can Redwood support HSM/KMS integration in Private or Dedicated?
[02:10] Priya Malhotra (SE): Yes — Redwood Private has customer-managed KMS integrations, Dedicated supports KMS via customer-managed keys in our cloud offering, and Hosted supports envelope encryption with Redwood-managed keys but we can discuss custom arrangements for Enterprise plans.
[02:28] Jordan: Just to set expectations, many customers start with Hosted for speed to value, then move to Dedicated when they need predictable throughput and lower unit cost, and Private when they require full network isolation or strict data residency. But each has tradeoffs.
[02:45] Ethan: Can you walk through the sizing math for Dedicated — what commit do we need for 120 QPS and those token lengths?
[02:55] Priya Malhotra (SE): Sure. Rough back-of-envelope: 120 QPS with average 160 tokens per call is about 19,200 tokens/sec, that's ~1.15M tokens/min, ~1.6B tokens/day if it's sustained — but you said spikes and not sustained. For Dedicated we size GPUs by peak concurrent sequences and sequence length; I'll share a sizing spreadsheet. We'll propose a baseline pool with autoscaling for spikes.
[03:20] Maya: That token math helps. Our budget constraints mean we likely can't commit to a huge reserved pool initially.
[03:28] Jordan: For the POC we usually run a 4-6 week pilot. A common pattern: week 0-1 onboarding + security review, week 1-3 run benchmarks and live traffic shadowing, week 3-4 iterate on prompts and measure quality/regressions, week 4-6 pilot evaluation and decision. Does that timeline work?
[03:50] Ethan: Yes, that seems reasonable. What's included in 'benchmarks'?
[03:55] Priya Malhotra (SE): We'll run an orchestrated harness: steady-state QPS tests, spike tests, latency distribution collection (p50/p95/p99), throughput per GPU, token/sec metrics, and A/B accuracy checks vs your current model. We'll use a sample prompt set you provide and also our standard evals. We'll share a GSheet with the test plan.
[04:18] Samir: If we run benchmarks on Hosted, will that be representative for Dedicated?
[04:22] Priya Malhotra (SE): Good question. Hosted gives you a baseline — same model variants but contention and multi-tenant factors can add variance. Dedicated will be more predictable and usually lower p95, depending on hardware. For strict comparability we can run the same harness on a Dedicated mirror for the POC; there may be cost for the dedicated test instance but we can size a small reserved pool for the run.
[04:45] Maya: What about Private? If we need Private for data residency or KMS, how long does setup take?
[04:52] Jordan: Private typically takes longer — customer-controlled VPC peering, on-prem packages or air-gapped installs can be multi-week. From contract to running tests usually 6-10 weeks depending on network and security approvals.
[05:05] Priya K (Security): For Private we need details on audit logging, separation of logs, and whether PII is ever exfiltrated to Redwood telemetry.
[05:13] Priya Malhotra (SE): We provide audit logs and can configure retention. Private gives you full control of telemetry; Dedicated also supports strict retention and enterprise log exports. For Hosted we can restrict what telemetry we keep but it's more limited. We'll include the security docs and SOC2 report.
[05:30] Jordan: On success criteria — Maya, you mentioned latency and accuracy. Anything else?
[05:34] Maya: Latency p95 under 800ms for common 200-token requests; throughput at peak with <2% error rate; and retrieval quality measured by our eval set — maintain or exceed baseline F1/ROUGE by X (we'll share numbers). Also cost target of < $Y per 1M tokens — we'll provide a budget range in the doc.
[05:55] Ethan: We also want good observability — token-level cost and per-route metrics, and the ability to A/B feed traffic if we do rollouts.
[06:05] Liam (Solutions): Redwood Console offers per-route dashboards, token-level cost breakdown, and rollout controls for canary and automatic fallback policies.
[06:15] Samir: For privacy, is there an option for local KV cache or we need to rely on Redwood's? There's concern about embedding caches storing customer vectors.
[06:25] Priya Malhotra (SE): You can opt to keep caches in your VPC on Private. For Dedicated we can configure cache persistence and retention policies; by default Hosted manages caches but we can disable retention for sensitive customers.
[06:38] Maya: About benchmarks — how do you measure AO of models when you have retrieval augmentation? Our RAG pipeline is a combination of embedding-based retrieval and LLM rewrite. We need to ensure the end-to-end latency includes retrieval.
[06:50] Priya Malhotra (SE): We'll run end-to-end benchmarks that include retrieval latencies. Recommend you provide a snapshot of your vector store or we can mock it with a realistic latency profile.
[07:05] Ethan: For the Dedicated cost model, what's the delta vs Hosted per token?
[07:10] Jordan: It varies a lot by commit and utilization. At low utilization Hosted can be cheaper due to no commit, but at steady high throughput Dedicated reduces per-token costs because of reserved GPU efficiency and ability to tune quantization. We'll provide example numbers in the pricing sheet.
[07:25] Maya: Can you support quantized model variants? We want lower cost mode for non-critical completions.
[07:30] Priya Malhotra (SE): Yes — Redwood supports quantization profiles and we can recommend model + quantization combos per workload in Redwood Optimize. That is part of the POC analysis.
[07:42] Jordan: Let's talk decision criteria — if you need network isolation + KMS + strict residency, Private; if you need predictable capacity and better unit economics, Dedicated; if you want fastest time-to-value and low upfront, Hosted. You might also choose a hybrid: start Hosted, then Dedicated with Private for regulated subsets.
[08:02] Maya: That hybrid path makes sense. For the pilot, we'd like to see Hosted baseline and a small Dedicated mirror test to compare.
[08:10] Priya Malhotra (SE): We can do that. We'll propose a minimal Dedicated footprint for the mirror — just enough GPUs to emulate your peak for short runs during the 2 week benchmarking window.
[08:22] Samir: On networking, for Dedicated do we need CIDR peering?
[08:25] Liam (Solutions): For our Dedicated in cloud we support VPC peering or private links depending on cloud provider. We'll include network playbooks.
[08:35] Priya K (Security): Also, for legal we might need a sub-processor list and data flow diagrams.
[08:40] Jordan: We'll attach the security pack and sub-processor list.
[08:45] Maya: A question on rollback — if a model rollout degrades accuracy, can we automate fallback?
[08:50] Priya Malhotra (SE): Yes, Redwood's rollout allows automatic fallback and canary metrics tied to evaluation prompts; you'll get alerts if quality dips.
[08:58] Ethan: For benchmarking metrics, can you capture token-level costs and map them to our billing?
[09:03] Priya Malhotra (SE): We'll provide token-level counters and a cost model; we'll map to approximate dollar costs per million tokens using both Hosted and Dedicated estimates.
[09:12] Jordan: Ok quick recap and next steps: Priya will send benchmark harness and prompts; Jordan will send pricing + Dedicated sizing; Samir will share traffic traces and token distribution; Maya will confirm success criteria and stakeholders. Aim to kick off onboarding week of 2026-03-09.
[09:35] Maya: Sounds good.
[09:37] Ethan: One last ask — can you include a sample SLA and uptime for Dedicated?
[09:41] Jordan: Yes we'll include sample SLA and list of support tiers.
[09:44] Priya K (Security): Please also include SOC2 and ISO certs.
[09:47] Jordan: Absolutely. We'll follow up with a single email with attachments and links: security pack, sizing sheet, benchmark plan, and proposed timeline.
[09:55] Maya: Thanks everyone, that was helpful.
[09:58] Jordan: Thanks all, we'll follow up.
[10:00] END OF RECORDING (approx 42m)
